result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` is now classified as mock resources (test code), at any depth and with either slash style. The new tests and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass offline.

**The change** is in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`. I replaced the two narrow mock rules (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) with one rule:

`(.*[/\\])?(__)?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`

The folder-name part is `[^/\\]*`, so any characters are allowed, including punctuation and non-ASCII. The match stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, and `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't either because they have no separator after the name. The existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` cases still match.

**The test** is a new file, `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/MockResourcesConventionTest.java`. It covers the elasticsearch case, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, backslash paths, the previously supported folders, and the negative cases. All 3 tests pass.

I did not touch the separate `[Mm]ocks/` and `mockapi/` rules, and I did not run a full build or install.
